items: First steps: new to a language? Short lessons of everyday phrases, starting from nothing, in 43 languages. You hear each phrase, write it and say it, and it then comes back in your review. Choose level A1 to see them first, or open them from the Library.

Letters and sounds: a chart of the letters to hear and practise for Japanese, Korean, Russian, Greek, Arabic, Hindi, Thai and seven more scripts, and a list of the sounds that surprise for French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Croatian and Chinese.
Record yourself when you speak, and hear your own take after the model's.
With a teacher: copy a sitting to send to a teacher or tutor (Progress), and type their corrections in so they come back in your review (Words).
LanguageLab installs like an app (Settings), and after one visit it opens without a connection.
Stories written by your AI agent now bring two sentences to write back from their meaning, like the ones that come with the app.

Eleven languages now come with stories: French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Croatian and English, and smaller sets for Chinese, Japanese and Korean. Any other language works with your own texts and with stories from AI cowork. Pick yours in Settings.
A sitting now asks you three questions after you have only heard the story, so you can see how much you follow by ear.
Speak: dialogues you play a part in. You read your lines aloud, then say them from memory.
Conversation: talk with an AI partner who answers and corrects you as you go. It runs on your device where the browser has its own AI model, and otherwise through your AI cowork folder.

Write it back: a sitting shows you what a sentence means and you write it in the language you are learning. It is marked word by word, and works in every browser for the stories that come with the app.
Grammar you have met: each text ends with one point to notice, and the Words screen keeps them all.
Pen pal: write a letter and an AI pen pal answers at your level and corrects you (through the AI cowork folder). Your corrected mistakes come back in review until you get them right.
Just listen plays stories one after another, and Read lets you read anything in your library with a tap for each new word. Both count as input.
Tap a word that has no meaning and, in Chrome or Edge on a computer, it is translated on your device. You can also translate the whole sentence, type your own meaning, or look the word up.
Progress now says which level your numbers support for reading and for listening, with a table level by level.
A Words screen: search your words, fix a meaning, say "I know this", or send a known word back to review.
Bring your own recording: add a podcast or video sound file with its subtitle file, and take dictation from the real voices.
More French: fourteen new stories up to C1, and fourteen dialogues up to B2.
Say it: after the dictation you read three sentences aloud, and the score is the share of your words that speech recognition understood (in browsers that have it).
Twelve more French stories, from A1 to B2. Today now offers the unread story closest to your level.
Progress draws your dictation scores sitting by sitting, and shows how well you were understood when reading aloud.
Leaving a sitting half way now warns you first, and keeps what you typed.
Colour themes: the shared list is in Settings, under Appearance.
Google sign-in is shared with the other apps, so you are not asked to pick your account again.

First version. A sitting takes one French story through four steps: listen without the text, read it and tap the words you don't know, take dictation at natural speed, then retell it in your own words.
The words you tap come back for review inside the sentence you met them in, and you type them.
Progress shows what you can do (words caught by ear, words understood, words produced from memory), with no points and no streak.
With an AI cowork folder, an agent writes new stories at your level and gives each sitting an honest grade.
